newsitem.title: NIGER: Three soldiers killed in Niger Tuareg clash.
newsitem.headline: Three soldiers killed in Niger Tuareg clash.

text.p: At least three soldiers were killed and a dozen wounded during a clash with Tuareg rebels in Niger's central Agadez region, military sources said.
Monday's clash, near the Baguezan hills 1,200 km north east of the capital Niamey, involved the Unified Resistance Movement (MUR), part of a coalition in peace moves with the government.
The sources said the soldiers died when their vehicle hit a mine during the clash. There was no official confirmation of the report.
The latest peace moves, agreed in early December, envisage 5,900 fighters reporting to assembly points.
Light-skinned Tuaregs, nomads of Berber descent, took up arms in 1990 in Niger and neighbouring Mali, denouncing domination by black-majority governments.
The main Tuareg rebel groups in Niger signed a peace deal in April 1995. A peace deal has quelled the revolt in Mali.
